subject: health
unitTitle: Substance Misuse Trends, Refusal Skills, and Support Pathways
title: Correction and reflection: treatment, recovery, and confidential support pathways
focus: treatment, recovery, and confidential support pathways
essentialQuestion: How do I hold a decision when the pressure is quiet, repeated, and from someone close?
materials: guardian-approved local and national support resource list
keyPoints: Treatment and recovery may include medical, counseling, peer, and community supports; access, confidentiality, and level of care vary, so a trusted professional can explain options.
Compare care options by function, access, safety, and sustainability; avoid appearance rules, shame, rigid perfection, or assumptions about another person’s habits.

For treatment, recovery, and confidential support pathways, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Build a support-pathway map for three fictional situations of escalating seriousness, naming the trusted adult, the service, and the point at which emergency help is called.
studentTask: Use the supplied fictional day to create a care plan for treatment, recovery, and confidential support pathways. Identify two needs or barriers, choose two feasible supports, and explain how each supports function or recovery without appearance rules, shame, or a requirement to reveal personal habits.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in treatment, recovery, and confidential support pathways; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the treatment, recovery, and confidential support pathways task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: The map may be drawn, listed, dictated, or completed on a supplied template. Reading load may be reduced with summarized resource descriptions.
extensionChallenge: Apply treatment, recovery, and confidential support pathways under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
